posts.title: The Salt Monopoly as a Universal Symbol
posts.body: Salt was taxed heavily by the British colonial state despite being consumed equally by rich and poor. Mahatma Gandhi identified it as the most oppressive tax on essential daily life.
posts.analogy: Taxing basic salt in 1930 was like taxing tap drinking water or air today: everyone felt the direct pain.

posts.title: Chronology of the March: 24 Days on Foot
posts.body: Starting on 12-Mar-1930 from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 trusted volunteers, walking 10 miles a day, arriving at the coastal village of Dandi on 05-Apr-1930 and breaking the law on 06-Apr-1930.
posts.analogy: A marching media campaign that rallied thousands of villagers along rural Gujarat highways.

posts.title: Board MCQ: Initial Volunteer Count
posts.body: How many trusted ashram volunteers accompanied Gandhiji at the start of the historic Salt March?

quiz.question: How many trusted volunteers began the march from Sabarmati Ashram?
quiz.explanation: Gandhiji started with 78 verified ashram members, though thousands joined as the procession traversed Gujarati villages.

posts.subject: SST

posts.title: Salt Satyagraha Across Coastal India
posts.body: C. Rajagopalachari led a parallel march from Trichinopoly to Vedarannyam in Tamil Nadu, and K. Kelappan led the march in Malabar (Kerala), breaking salt laws coast to coast.
posts.analogy: A decentralized nationwide movement synchronized without modern social media.
posts.subject: SST

posts.title: CBSE Distinction: Non-Cooperation vs Civil Disobedience
posts.body: In 1920-22 (Non-Cooperation), people were asked not to cooperate with the colonial government. In 1930 (Civil Disobedience), people were urged to actively BREAK colonial laws like salt and forest laws.
posts.subject: SST

posts.title: Mid-Feed Check: Why CDM Was Distinctive
posts.body: 1. Large-scale participation of women picketing liquor and foreign cloth shops. 2. Active defiance of statutory colonial regulations. 3. Boycott of British revenue and village chaukidari taxes.
posts.analogy: Escalation from passive boycotting to active civic resistance.
posts.subject: SST

posts.title: Board MCQ: Gandhi-Irwin Pact Year
posts.body: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed, leading to the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement?

quiz.question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed in London/Delhi?
quiz.explanation: Signed on 5 March 1931, Viceroy Irwin agreed to release political prisoners in exchange for Congress participating in the Second Round Table Conference.

posts.subject: SST

posts.title: Revision Summary: Civil Disobedience Movement
posts.body: The 1930 Dandi March mobilized ordinary Indians across caste, class, and gender against colonial salt tax exploitation. By demonstrating the power of mass satyagraha, it marked a decisive turning point towards complete independence (Purna Swaraj).
